doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

title: Fitting into many genres, grown up in Philadelphia
summary: Rowe reads an All Music Guide description; Brecker says Philly's mix of styles made versatility natural and aimed him at freelancing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. And I’m up at Hamilton College in Clinton, New York. I’d like to do a little introduction but you’ve done too many things. So I have the All Music Guide to Jazz. Now this is 25 years old but here’s what it says about Randy Brecker. “Randy Brecker is essentially a fine hard bop trumpet soloist, but one versatile enough to fit into nearly any setting including the pop world, funk bands, and electronic fusion.” Anything you’d like to add?

Well it’s just that it’s not that hard to fit into other genres as some people think. You know I just came up listening to a lot of different styles of music, being from Philly, which was a potpourri of all different styles of music, musicians, it was wonderful to see that. And I grew up with that mindset and with the goal of kind of I guess being a freelance musician in New York, for lack of a better way to put it.
